citation: This work (AF-Q86TW2 v6 vs PDB 5I35 chain A)
claim: ADCK1 adopts the COQ8A protein-kinase-like fold
key_finding: TM-align-style superposition: TM-score 0.816, core RMSD 2.26 A over 299 residue pairs (381 aligned). ADCK1 mean pLDDT 83.7 overall, 91.5 for residues 100-400, 90.9 for the mapped ATP-site residues (min 81.1).
context: AlphaFold DB model of human ADCK1 vs COQ8A R611K + AMP-PNP crystal structure
confidence: High for the fold; model-based, so side-chain rotamers are predictions, not observations

key_finding: 11 of 12 COQ8A sites identical in ADCK1 (K276/Q279 KxGQ, A339/S340 A-rich loop, K358 beta3, E411 alphaC, E446 hinge, D488 catalytic loop, N493 Mg-Asn, D507/G509). Only F508 differs (His in ADCK1). Score equals yeast Coq8 and E. coli UbiB (11/12); ADCK2 scores 7/12.
context: Gotoh affine-gap alignment, BLOSUM62, anchored on human COQ8A Q8NI60
confidence: High; pairwise alignment identity to COQ8A is only 27%, so individual column assignments were cross-checked structurally

claim: Seed hypothesis residue numbering is correct
key_finding: Direct 1-based UniProt check: K102-V103-G104-Q105 is the ADCK1 KxGQ motif; A164 is the A-rich loop Ala (TPLGTAS-LAQVH), not a KxGQ residue; K183 is the beta3 Lys (RTVAVKVQH); D315 is the catalytic-loop Asp (GFVHCDPHPGN); D338-H339-G340 is the DFG-like triad, so ADCK1 has DHG where COQ8A has DFG.
confidence: High; direct sequence read. The seed hypothesis mislabels A164 as part of the KxGQ motif

claim: An ATP-sized pocket is assembled in ADCK1
key_finding: AMP-PNP transplanted from 5I35 into the superposed models gives 6 heavy-atom contacts under 2.2 A in ADCK1, against 2 in the COQ8A AlphaFold model, 1 COQ8B, 4 ADCK5, 4 yeast Coq8, 6 Cqd2, 9 ADCK2, 10 UbiB, 12 Cqd1 and 33 in the apo COQ8A crystal 4PED (positive control for a collapsed pocket).
context: Rigid-body ligand transplant, no side-chain repacking
confidence: Moderate; a rigid transplant overstates clashes, and the apo-4PED control shows the assay separates open from closed pockets but does not measure affinity

claim: The beta3 Lys to alphaC Glu ion pair is formed
key_finding: ADCK1 K183 NZ to E236 OE1 = 2.73 A, against 2.80 A for COQ8A K358 NZ to E411 OE2 in 5I35.
confidence: Moderate; salt bridges are a feature AlphaFold models reliably, but this is a prediction

claim: The KxGQ/A-rich elements occlude the substrate groove
key_finding: PKI(5-24) peptide transferred by ligand-anchored superposition (30 shared nucleotide heavy atoms, RMSD 0.88 A) clashes with ADCK1 T99, K102, V103, Q105, H106, K123, H126, L219, V220, A223, D315, H317, P318 (87 contacts) and with COQ8A K276, L277, Q279 in 5I35 (94 contacts). Control: PKA chain E against its own PKI peptide gives 0 clashes.
context: Ligand-anchored transfer; sequence-seeded superposition onto PKA failed (TM 0.19-0.28) and was discarded
confidence: Moderate; shows the canonical peptide path is blocked, and says nothing about a non-peptide substrate

claim: The mapped positions are under purifying selection in metazoa
key_finding: 91 filtered metazoan ADCK1 orthologs (OrthoDB 6324708at33208, best-hit filtered against all five human paralogs): 17 of 20 motif positions are >=95% identical against a 30.6% background rate. Binomial p = 7.3e-07; Mann-Whitney U = 4970, p = 4.5e-09.
context: OrthoDB metazoan group, 4579 records reduced to 91 confident ADCK1 orthologs
confidence: High for conservation; conservation of a nucleotide pocket does not by itself prove phosphotransfer

claim: COQ8A is the right functional reference for ADCK1
key_finding: ADCK1 full-length identity: ADCK5 39.3%, yeast Cqd2 35.4%, Cqd1 29.5%, COQ8B 28.8%, ADCK2 27.5%, COQ8A 27.2%, yeast Coq8 25.4%, UbiB 24.8%. The COQ8 clade is internally tight (COQ8A-COQ8B 60.3%, COQ8A-Coq8y 41.1%). ADCK1 sits with ADCK5 and Cqd2.
context: All-against-all Gotoh alignment of nine UbiB proteins
confidence: High; ADCK1 is not a COQ8 ortholog, so COQ8A supplies a structural template and not a functional assignment

claim: COQ8A binds nucleotide through the mapped residues
key_finding: COQ8A structures define the KxGQ domain and A-rich loop; mutations K358R abolish and D507N strongly impair ADP/ATP binding (UniProt Q8NI60 ECO:0000269).
context: Human COQ8A, recombinant protein and crystallography
confidence: High for COQ8A; transfer to ADCK1 is inference

claim: The A-rich loop controls nucleotide selectivity and catalysis
key_finding: COQ8A A339G enables autophosphorylation but inhibits coenzyme Q biosynthesis in vivo; yeast Coq8 A197G/A197S abolish CoQ biosynthesis while retaining cis autophosphorylation.
context: Human COQ8A and S. cerevisiae Coq8
confidence: High; shows the A-rich loop is a real functional element, and that unlocking protein-kinase-like activity breaks the native function

claim: UbiB-family proteins are ATPases rather than protein kinases
key_finding: COQ8A activity is better described as a lipid-stimulated ATPase; mutations at E411, D488 and N493 impair ADP/ATP binding (UniProt Q8NI60 ECO:0000269).
confidence: High for COQ8A; this reframes 'catalytically competent' away from protein phosphotransfer

claim: ADCK1 catalytic residues are required for its function
key_finding: Drosophila/mammalian ADCK1 acts through YME1L1 on OPA1 and IMMT to control mitochondrial dynamics and cristae. UniProt Q86TW2 records A164G, K183I and D315A each with 'No effect on role in maintaining mitochondrial structure and function' (ECO:0000269), and the FUNCTION comment states ADCK1 acts 'in a kinase-independent manner'.
context: Drosophila melanogaster muscle, plus mammalian cell overexpression
confidence: High for the assay performed; readout was mitochondrial morphology and function, not nucleotide binding or phosphotransfer

key_finding: Drosophila ADCK1 mutants die as second instar larvae with double mouth hooks and tracheal breaks; tracheal rescue restores viability; mutants have normal levels of basic metabolites. No CoQ biosynthesis defect reported.
confidence: High; argues against importing the COQ8 function into ADCK1

claim: The atypical kinase/ATPase domain is required in the ADCK1 clade
key_finding: Yeast Cqd1 (Ypl109c) and Cqd2 (Ylr253w) reciprocally control cellular CoQ distribution, and 'the activities of both proteins rely on their atypical kinase/ATPase domains, which they share with Coq8'.
context: S. cerevisiae genetics, fractionation and lipid profiling
confidence: High; Cqd2 is ADCK1's closest yeast relative in this set, so this is the most relevant functional precedent

claim: ADCK1-clade proteins act at membrane contact sites
key_finding: Cqd1 is an inner-membrane protein forming a contact site with the outer-membrane proteins Por1 and Om14, and is involved in phospholipid homeostasis; CQD1/CQD2 overexpression tethers mitochondria to the ER.
confidence: Moderate for ADCK1; Cqd1 is the ADCK2 relative, Cqd2 the ADCK1 relative, so the clade assignment matters

claim: ADCK1 is an active protein kinase with substrates
key_finding: Phospho-PCA pooled screening with the KINBERT model identified 'novel high-confidence substrates for 23 kinase constructs representing 21 distinct kinases, including the understudied dark kinases ADCK1 and CaMKK1'.
context: Pooled reporter assay in cells, kinase construct plus substrate peptide library
confidence: Low to moderate for ADCK1 specifically; a complementation screen reports phosphorylation of a reporter and does not establish direct phosphotransfer by purified ADCK1. Needs the full text and per-kinase controls before use

claim: Existing annotation supports ADCK1 kinase function
key_finding: 8 GO annotations, none MF. BP: GO:0007005 (IBA), GO:0010637 (IMP, PMID:31125351), GO:0055088 (IBA), GO:1903852 (IMP, PMID:31125351). CC: GO:0005739 (IDA, PMID:33988507), GO:0005743 (IBA). UniProt ATP-binding sites 161-169 and 183 and active site 315 all carry ECO:0000255 from PROSITE-ProRule PRU00159.
context: Database records, retrieved via the QuickGO API
confidence: High that the records say this; the MF features are rule-based transfer and are not independent evidence

key_finding: Review of ADCK1-ADCK5 describing them as putative mitochondrial proteins 'believed to play a role in' CoQ biosynthesis, energy production and cellular metabolism.
confidence: Orientation only; review-level, hedged language, no new primary data on ADCK1 catalysis
